quickSummary: The plasma membrane is a dynamic quasi-fluid lipid bilayer (Singer & Nicolson, 1972). Phosphoglycerides have hydrophilic polar heads facing water and hydrophobic tails facing inward. Integral transmembrane proteins span the bilayer; peripheral proteins bind electrostatically. Lipid transbilayer flip-flop is catalyzed by ATP-dependent Flippase (inward) and Floppase (outward), and ATP-independent Scramblase. Transport occurs via simple diffusion, facilitated channels/aquaporins, and primary active P-type Na+/K+ ATPase (pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3. The Fluid Mosaic Model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3. The Fluid Mosaic Model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972)

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Lipids provide a fluid matrix; proteins float as a mosaic. Flip-flop movement is slow and enzyme-dependent (Flippase/Floppase/Scramblase).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FLUID MOSAIC MODEL OVERVIEW
                           
                      [ Glycoprotein / Glycolipid ] (Extracellular)
                                   │
              O   O   O   O   O   O   O   O   O  <-- Hydrophilic Polar Heads
              ││  ││  ││  ││  ││  ││  ││  ││  ││ <-- Hydrophobic Non-Polar Fatty Acid Tails
              O   O   O   O   O   O   O   O   O  <-- Hydrophilic Polar Heads
                          │               │
                   [ Integral ]    [ Peripheral ]
                    Protein          Protein
conceptBreakdown.content:
The biological membrane is a dynamic, quasi-fluid phospholipid bilayer studded with mosaic protein complexes.

### Membrane Components
• **Lipid Matrix**: Primarily **Phosphoglycerides** (amphipathic molecules with hydrophilic polar heads exposed to water and hydrophobic non-polar hydrocarbon tails shielded in the interior).
• **Fluidity Buffers**: Fluidity is regulated by unsaturated fatty acids and sterols (**Cholesterol** in animals, **Ergosterol** in fungi, **Phytosterols** in plants, and **Hopanoids** in eubacteria).
• **Protein Classes**:
  1. **Peripheral (Extrinsic) Proteins** (30%): Loosely attached to membrane surfaces via electrostatic interactions; readily extracted by mild salt buffers.
  2. **Integral (Intrinsic) Proteins** (70%): Embedded deeply in the hydrophobic core; transmembrane proteins cross the bilayer via $\alpha$-helical hydrophobic spans (*e.g., Glycophorins, Aquaporins, Porins*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.1 Transbilayer Lipid Movement (Flip-Flop)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.1 Transbilayer Lipid Movement (Flip-Flop)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TRANSBILAYER LIPID MOVEMENT (FLIP-FLOP)
                      
   FLIPPASE: ATP-dependent; moves lipids from Outer ──► Inner (Cytosolic) Leaflet
   FLOPPASE: ATP-dependent; moves lipids from Inner ──► Outer Leaflet
   SCRAMBLASE: ATP-independent; bi-directionally scrambles lipids down concentration gradient
conceptBreakdown.content:
While lateral diffusion of lipids within the same leaflet is extremely rapid, spontaneous transbilayer ('flip-flop') movement between leaflets is thermodynamically unfavorable and slow. Cells employ specific enzymes:
• **Flippase**: P-type ATPase that utilizes ATP to move phospholipids from outer to inner (cytosolic) leaflet.
• **Floppase**: ABC transporter that uses ATP to move lipids from inner to outer leaflet.
• **Scramblase**: Calcium-activated, ATP-independent enzyme that scrambles lipids bidirectionally down concentration gradients.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Biophysical Membrane Transport Mechanisms
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Biophysical Membrane Transport Mechanisms
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MEMBRANE TRANSPORT MODES
                                        │
         ┌──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                             ▼
  PASSIVE TRANSPORT (No ATP)                                    ACTIVE TRANSPORT (ATP Used)
 ├── Simple Diffusion (Non-polar solutes down gradient)         ├── Primary Active ($Na^+/K^+$ ATPase Pump)
 └── Facilitated Diffusion (Polar solutes via Channels/Carriers) └── Secondary Active (SGLT Symport / Antiport)
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Passive Transport** (No ATP expenditure):
   - **Simple Diffusion**: Small non-polar molecules ($\text{O}_2, \text{CO}_2, \text{N}_2$, steroid hormones) diffuse directly through the lipid bilayer down their concentration gradient.
   - **Facilitated Diffusion**: Polar or charged solutes ($\text{Na}^+, \text{K}^+, \text{Cl}^-$, glucose, water via **Aquaporin** channels) cross via selective transport proteins (exhibiting saturation kinetics $V_{\max}$).
2. **Primary Active Transport ($Na^+/K^+$ ATPase Pump)**:
   - A P-type ATPase pump that hydrolyzes 1 molecule of ATP to pump **$3\text{ Na}^+$ OUT of the cell** and **$2\text{ K}^+$ INTO the cell**, establishing the negative resting membrane potential.
3. **Bulk Vesicular Transport**:
   - **Endocytosis**: Phagocytosis ('cell eating' of solids) and Pinocytosis ('cell drinking' of fluids).
   - **Exocytosis**: Fusion of secretory vesicles with the plasma membrane to discharge cargo outside.
